title: New Hope for Patients: Pig Kidneys Used as a Bridge to Human Transplants
subtitle: Medical researchers successfully use genetically modified animal organs to keep patients alive while they wait for human donors.

summary.en: Medical researchers have successfully used genetically modified pig kidneys to keep patients alive while they wait for human organ transplants. This new method acts as a bridge, allowing patients who are too sick to survive the wait to stay healthy. One patient, Tim Andrews, reported feeling much better after receiving a modified pig kidney. Experts believe this technology could eventually help solve the global shortage of human organs. While more testing is required, the company behind the project hopes to make these organs widely available within four years.
summary.zh: 醫學研究人員已成功利用基因改造豬腎，讓病患在等待人類器官移植期間維持生命。這種新方法扮演了過渡橋樑的角色，讓病情過重而無法等待的病患能保持健康。其中一名病患安德魯斯表示，在接受改造豬腎後感覺好轉許多。專家認為，這項技術最終可能有助於解決全球人類器官短缺的問題。儘管仍需更多測試，但該計畫背後的公司希望在四年內能廣泛提供這些器官。

paragraphs.en: For many people suffering from kidney failure, the wait for a life-saving transplant can be a race against time. Many patients become too sick to wait for a human organ donor, and traditional treatments like dialysis—a medical process that cleans the blood when kidneys stop working—are not always enough to keep them alive. However, a recent medical breakthrough is offering new hope. According to NPR, surgeons have successfully used genetically modified pig kidneys to keep two patients alive long enough to eventually receive human kidney transplants.
paragraphs.zh: 對於許多腎衰竭患者而言，等待救命的器官移植往往是一場與時間的賽跑。許多病患因病情過重，無法等到人類器官捐贈者，而傳統治療方式如洗腎（一種在腎臟停止運作時用來淨化血液的醫療程序）也未必足以維持生命。然而，近期的一項醫療突破帶來了新希望。根據美國公共廣播電台（NPR）報導，外科醫師已成功利用基因改造豬腎，讓兩名病患維持生命，直到他們最終能接受人類腎臟移植。

paragraphs.en: One of the patients, 66-year-old Tim Andrews from New Hampshire, faced a difficult situation. His doctors told him that his kidneys had failed and that he might not live for another year. He was struggling with his health and felt that he had very few options left. When he heard about a research project in Boston involving pig kidneys that were changed at a genetic level to work in human bodies, he decided to volunteer. He explained that he wanted to help humanity, even if the treatment did not save him personally.
paragraphs.zh: 其中一名患者是來自新罕布夏州、六十六歲的安德魯斯（Tim Andrews），他當時面臨艱難的處境。醫師告知他的腎臟已經衰竭，恐怕活不過一年。他當時健康狀況惡化，感覺幾乎走投無路。當他聽說波士頓有一項研究計畫，涉及將豬腎進行基因層面的改造以使其能在人體內運作時，他決定自願參與。他表示，即便這項治療無法親自救他一命，他也希望能為人類做出貢獻。

paragraphs.en: NPR reports that after receiving the modified pig kidney in January 2025, Andrews felt much better almost immediately. He was no longer tied to a dialysis machine and felt strong enough to walk around again. He even gave the pig kidney a nickname, "Wilma." While the pig kidney eventually stopped working after about nine months, it served its purpose as a vital bridge. It kept Andrews alive and healthy until a human kidney became available three months later. Since receiving his human transplant, Andrews says he is back to enjoying his life, including swimming and riding his bike.
paragraphs.zh: NPR 報導指出，安德魯斯在二零二五年一月接受改造豬腎後，幾乎立即感到好轉。他不再需要依賴洗腎機，且體力恢復到足以再次四處走動。他甚至為這顆豬腎取了個綽號叫「威瑪」（Wilma）。雖然這顆豬腎在約九個月後停止運作，但它成功發揮了關鍵的過渡作用。它讓安德魯斯在等待三個月後獲得人類腎臟前，得以維持生命與健康。自從接受人類器官移植後，安德魯斯表示他已重拾生活樂趣，包括游泳與騎腳踏車。

paragraphs.en: This development is part of a larger effort to address the severe shortage of organs available for transplant. Dr. Muhammad Mohiuddin, a researcher at the University of Maryland who was not involved in this specific study, noted that these results are very encouraging. He explained that while the long-term goal is to use animal organs as a permanent solution, the immediate priority is to ensure patients survive long enough to receive a human organ. This new method of using animal organs as a temporary support system is exactly what many patients need to stay alive during the waiting period.
paragraphs.zh: 這項進展是解決器官移植嚴重短缺問題的更大努力之一。並未參與此項特定研究的馬里蘭大學研究員莫希丁醫師（Dr. Muhammad Mohiuddin）指出，這些結果非常令人振奮。他解釋說，雖然長遠目標是將動物器官作為永久解決方案，但當務之急是確保病患能存活足夠長的時間以接受人類器官。這種將動物器官作為臨時支持系統的新方法，正是許多病患在等待期間維持生命所需要的。

paragraphs.en: EGenesis, the biotech company responsible for developing these modified pig organs, says that another patient has also been kept alive using this method until a human transplant could be performed. The company is optimistic about the future of this technology, though they emphasize that much more testing is required before it can be used on a larger scale. They hope to make these genetically modified pig kidneys available to more hospitals and patients within about four years.
paragraphs.zh: 負責開發這些改造豬器官的生物科技公司 eGenesis 表示，另一名病患也透過此方法維持生命，直到成功進行人類器官移植。該公司對這項技術的未來持樂觀態度，但也強調在進行大規模應用前，仍需進行更多測試。他們希望在四年內，能讓更多醫院與病患取得這些基因改造豬腎。

paragraphs.en: This medical advancement represents a significant step forward in transplant science. By using genetic modification to make pig organs compatible with the human body, scientists are finding ways to overcome the biological barriers that previously made such transplants impossible. The success of these two cases provides a clear path for future research. If the technology continues to prove safe and effective, it could change the lives of thousands of people who are currently waiting for a transplant.
paragraphs.zh: 這項醫療進展代表了移植科學的一大躍進。透過基因改造使豬器官與人體相容，科學家正設法克服過去導致此類移植無法實現的生物障礙。這兩個案例的成功，為未來研究提供了明確的方向。若該技術持續證明安全有效，將能改變成千上萬名目前正在等待移植者的生命。

paragraphs.en: As the medical community looks toward the future, the focus will remain on safety and long-term results. While the idea of using animal organs might seem unusual to some, the success stories of patients like Andrews show that it can be a life-saving bridge. For those who have run out of other options, this technology offers a second chance at life. As researchers continue to refine these methods, the hope is that the wait for a transplant will no longer be a death sentence for so many patients around the world.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著醫學界展望未來，焦點仍將放在安全性與長期成效上。雖然使用動物器官的概念對某些人來說可能顯得不尋常，但像安德魯斯這樣的成功案例顯示，這能成為救命的橋樑。對於那些已無其他選擇的病患而言，這項技術提供了第二次生命機會。隨著研究人員持續改良這些方法，人們期盼等待移植對全球許多病患來說，將不再等同於被判死刑。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To be forced to stay in a specific place or connected to a specific thing, often limiting one's freedom.
keyTerms.noteZh: 這裡指患者必須依賴機器，無法自由活動。文中：He was no longer tied to a dialysis machine and felt strong enough to walk around again.

keyTerms.definitionEn: Something that acts as a connection or a temporary solution between two states or events.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見指實體的橋，這裡比喻為過渡性的醫療手段。文中：While the pig kidney eventually stopped working after about nine months, it served its purpose as a vital bridge.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To have nothing left of something.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見於日常對話，但在醫療語境下指沒有其他治療選擇。文中：For those who have run out of other options, this technology offers a second chance at life.

quiz.question: What was the primary role of the genetically modified pig kidney in Tim Andrews' medical journey?

options.A: It served as a permanent replacement for his failed kidneys.
options.B: It acted as a temporary support system until a human organ became available.
options.C: It was used to test whether human bodies could reject pig organs over several years.
options.D: It allowed him to avoid surgery by naturally repairing his own kidneys.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第三段，該豬腎臟被描述為「a vital bridge」（關鍵橋樑），其目的是讓 Andrews 保持健康，直到三個月後獲得人類腎臟移植。選項 A 錯誤，因為文章第四段提到長期目標才是永久解決方案，目前僅為臨時手段。選項 C 錯誤，因為該腎臟僅運作了九個月，並非測試多年排斥反應。選項 D 錯誤，因為文章明確指出他的腎臟已經衰竭，豬腎臟是移植而非修復。

quiz.question: Based on the information provided, why might some patients currently waiting for a kidney transplant be at high risk of death?

options.A: Because dialysis is no longer effective for any patient with kidney failure.
options.B: Because they are often allergic to the genetic modifications used in pig organs.
options.C: Because their condition may deteriorate to the point where they cannot survive the wait for a donor.
options.D: Because hospitals have stopped performing human-to-human kidney transplants.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據第一段，許多患者在等待捐贈器官時病情惡化（too sick to wait），而傳統的透析治療並不總是足夠維持生命，因此這項新技術能提供過渡期的支持。選項 A 過於絕對，文章僅說透析「不總是足夠」。選項 B 在文中未提及患者對基因改造過敏。選項 D 與事實相反，人類移植仍是最終目標，並未停止。

quiz.question: In the final paragraph, the author writes that the hope is that the wait for a transplant will no longer be a 'death sentence' for patients. What does 'death sentence' mean in this context?

options.A: A legal punishment issued by a court of law.
options.B: A situation that will almost certainly lead to death.
options.C: A medical diagnosis that is always wrong.
options.D: A formal document describing the causes of organ failure.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。在此語境下，「death sentence」是一種隱喻，指由於器官短缺導致患者在等待期間幾乎無法存活，最終走向死亡。選項 A 是該詞的字面法律意義，但在文中並非指法庭判決。選項 C 與 D 均與文章內容無關，且不符合該片語在英語中的慣用含義。

quiz.question: What is the central message of the article?

options.A: Genetically modified pig kidneys are now the preferred choice over human organs for all patients.
options.B: The biotech company EGenesis has solved the global organ shortage crisis completely.
options.C: Medical science is making progress in using modified animal organs to bridge the gap for transplant patients.
options.D: Tim Andrews is the only person in history who has successfully received a pig organ transplant.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章整體在討論如何透過基因改造豬器官作為過渡，解決器官短缺導致患者在等待期間死亡的問題。選項 A 錯誤，因為豬器官目前僅作為臨時橋樑。選項 B 誇大了事實，文章提到仍需更多測試且僅處於發展階段。選項 D 錯誤，文章第五段明確提到還有另一位患者也使用了此方法。
